raw_response:
I will do it the way I usually judge my land: start from what I did last year, look at what the nearby farmers got right, and not gamble too much. On 10.9 mu with just two people at home, I cannot spread myself too thin, so I will keep the wheat-maize as the main part, then put the rest into eggplant, tomato, and watermelon where I can watch them closely and use the well when the sky stays dry. For wheat and maize, I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because if the yield falls, that hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer money. For the vegetables and watermelon, I will feed them a bit heavier because those crops pull hard and I have seen thin fertilizer give thin fruit. I will still keep costs in mind, so I will not chase fancy things just because someone says so. I will mostly do what worked before: solid base manure and compound fertilizer, enough topdressing, enough water at the key times, and spray when I see real pressure. Neighbors around here who get steady harvests do not farm too lightly, and I will follow that road.
